answer: Ferrous Inlet Marking: each agent gets a hardware-embedded ferrous tag at its first inlet into the network, and the tag's magnetic signature is logged per transaction. Duplicating an identity forces reuse of the same tag signature, which the ledger flags as a conflicting twin. An attacker must forge distinct physical tags per identity, paying fabrication and provisioning cost far above the value of one extra agent. The jetty process (onboarding gate) rejects any signature already seen.
